_comment: Vetted, human-verified exceptions for tools/ci/reconcile-assertion-ledgers.py. Every entry names the evidence a reader can re-check; there is no unexplained entry. Keyed by (ledger file, cited file, cited line) exactly as the ledger's own first table column reads it -- do not add an entry without reading both the ledger's own prose and the source line(s) involved.

equivalences.reason: guard-line-vs-assert-line citation convention (§1b): the ledger's first column cites the shared aabb_intersection guard's own production line (tools.rs:68, `if min[0] >= max[0] || min[1] >= max[1] || min[2] >= max[2]`) once per axis-isolating test (rows suffixed (x)/(y)/(z)), rather than each test's own assert!(...).is_empty()) line. The three real scanner sites those tests exercise are tools.rs:259 (boxes_that_only_touch_do_not_intersect), tools.rs:271 (boxes_that_only_touch_on_y_do_not_intersect), tools.rs:283 (boxes_that_only_touch_on_z_do_not_intersect) -- confirmed by reading the ledger's own §1b prose (which states this explicitly: 'tools.rs:259,271,283 are the same physical lines as existing rows tools.rs:68 (x)/(y)/(z), not new sites') and by reading tools.rs itself to verify each test's body and its one assert! line. Naive file:line matching manufactures three false orphans here; this is the one instance of the guard-line-citation trap this instrument was asked to encode.
